title: Quantity Comparison
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Quantity Comparison. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Use common denominators and cross multiplication

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Numerical comparisons

To compare fractions with positive denominators, use a common denominator or cross multiplication. For decimals, align place values. For negative values, the number closer to zero is greater.

Ratios, rates and percentages

Convert quantities to common units before comparing. Compare a rate using the same denominator or calculate unit rates. A percent is a fraction out of 100, so percent comparisons depend on their stated bases.

Algebraic comparisons

When quantities contain variables, record the domain and sign assumptions first. A comparison may vary with the variable; test critical values or derive an inequality. Do not choose one quantity as greater from a single convenient example.

Worked example: Compare (\(3/7\)) and (\(4/9\)). Cross products are (\(3 \times 9=27\)) and (\(4 \times 7=28\)), so (\(3/7<4/9\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Check units before comparing distances, prices or rates.
  • For positive fractions, cross multiply; if denominators can be negative, first account for their signs.
  • Estimate nearby benchmark values such as (\(1/2\)), 1 and 100%.
  • For variable expressions, test boundaries and sign changes rather than one sample value.
  • Keep equality as a possible outcome unless strict inequality is proved.

  4. Standard:

    Which is the better unit price: 750 g for Rs 90 or 1 kg for Rs 116?

    2. 1 kg pack

    Answer: 1 kg pack

    First pack costs (\(90/0.75=Rs 120\)) per kg; the second costs Rs 116 per kg, so the 1 kg pack is cheaper.
